item.title: TT-104: Undo
item.brief:
Operator request: implement ticket TT-104 from BACKLOG.md in the tasktracker package (repo subdir tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Use only the standard library. Keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, and add tests for this ticket. Commit only this ticket, with a commit message naming TT-104 (as the git identity already configured in the repo; no attribution lines about AI tools). Acceptance criteria, exactly:

`tasktracker.store.TaskStore` has `add`, `complete` and `delete`. Add `undo()`:
- It reverts the most recent not-yet-undone `add`, `complete` or `delete`; repeated calls walk further back (LIFO), across all three kinds.
- Undoing an `add` removes that task; undoing a `complete` makes the task open again; undoing a `delete` restores the task exactly as it was, under the same id.
- Ids are never reused, even after undoing an `add`.
- With nothing left to undo, `undo()` raises `NothingToUndo` (defined in `tasktracker.store`).
- Failed operations (e.g. completing an unknown id) are not recorded.

Only edit what this ticket needs. Other tickets (TT-101, TT-102, TT-103) are being done in parallel by other items; do not implement them.

item.title: TT-103: Search query syntax
item.brief:
Operator request: implement ticket TT-103 from BACKLOG.md in the tasktracker package (repo subdir tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Use only the standard library. Keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, and add tests for this ticket. Commit only this ticket, with a commit message naming TT-103 (as the git identity already configured in the repo; no attribution lines about AI tools). Acceptance criteria, exactly:

`tasktracker.search.search(tasks, query)` only does a case-sensitive substring match on titles. Support a small query language instead:
- The query is split into terms on whitespace, except inside double quotes: `"fix login"` is one phrase term. All terms must match (AND).
- A bare word or phrase matches when it appears in the title, case-insensitively.
- `tag:NAME` matches tasks that have the tag NAME (exact tag, case-insensitive).
- `status:open` / `status:done` match on status.
- Any other `field:value` term, an unknown status, or an unterminated quote raises `QueryError` (defined in `tasktracker.search`).
- An empty or blank query matches every task. Results keep the input order.

Only edit what this ticket needs. Other tickets (TT-101, TT-102, TT-104) are being done in parallel by other items; do not implement them.

agt_01M88PF3BGFV6YXW8FSXEGD1H7:1.description: Field names are case-sensitive: TAG:work and Status:done raise QueryError 'unknown field'. The spec only fixes tag/status values as case-insensitive, so this is a defensible reading. Confirm it is intended, and consider a test pinning it.

agt_01M88PF3BGFV6YXW8FSXEGD1H7:2.description: An empty phrase "" parses to a text term with value '' and matches every task. Blank-query behaviour is specified, but an empty quoted phrase is not. Decide whether it should match everything or raise QueryError, and add a test for the choice.

agt_01M88PF3BGFV6YXW8FSXEGD1H7:3.description: Quotes are stripped anywhere in a term, so foo"bar baz" becomes the text 'foobar baz' and "a"b becomes 'ab'. Quotes mid-word are neither rejected nor treated as separators. Consider raising QueryError for quotes that do not open a whole term. No test covers this.

agt_01M88PF3BGFV6YXW8FSXEGD1H7:4.description: _split_terms has no assertions, and _unquote removes every double quote from a value (tag:"a""b" style input). The CLAUDE.md guidance asks for at least two meaningful assertions per non-trivial function; a cheap postcondition such as every raw term being non-empty would help.

agt_01M88PF3BGFV6YXW8FSXEGD1H7:5.description: Phrase matching is literal, so "fix login" with two spaces matches nothing even though the title has one space between the words. This matches the spec's literal-phrase reading, but it is worth noting in the docs.

agt_01M88PF3BGFV6YXW8FSXEGD1H7:6.description: Existing docstrings and comments are minimal, and there is no user-facing documentation for the query syntax (README only says search exists). Consider a short section listing the syntax.

risk.why: Behaviour change to search() (contained behind the existing interface) with a new QueryError path; only caller is test_basic.py, which passes. Reviewer rated medium.

item.title: TT-102: RFC 4180 CSV export
item.brief:
Operator request: implement ticket TT-102 from BACKLOG.md in the tasktracker package (repo subdir tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Use only the standard library. Keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, and add tests for this ticket. Commit only this ticket, with a commit message naming TT-102 (as the git identity already configured in the repo; no attribution lines about AI tools). Acceptance criteria, exactly:

`tasktracker.export.to_csv(tasks)` joins fields with commas and breaks on titles containing commas, quotes or newlines. It must produce RFC 4180 CSV:
- Header `id,title,tags,status,due`; one row per task in the given order.
- Tags joined with `;`, due date as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty.
- A field containing a comma, double quote, CR or LF is wrapped in double quotes, with embedded double quotes doubled. Other fields are not quoted.
- Every line (header included) ends with CRLF.

item.title: TT-101: Reject impossible due dates
item.brief:
Operator request: implement ticket TT-101 from BACKLOG.md in the tasktracker package (repo subdir tasktracker/, tests in tests/). Use only the standard library. Keep existing tests passing with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`, and add tests for this ticket. Commit only this ticket, with a commit message naming TT-101 (as the git identity already configured in the repo; no attribution lines about AI tools). Acceptance criteria, exactly:

`tasktracker.dates.parse_due(text, today)` silently clamps impossible dates: `2026-02-30` becomes `2026-02-28`. Instead:
- An impossible calendar date (`2026-02-30`, `2025-02-29`, `2026-04-31`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-00-10`) raises `InvalidDate`, a `ValueError` subclass defined in `tasktracker.dates`, whose message contains the original text.
- Anything else that does not match a supported form also raises `InvalidDate` (today it raises a bare `ValueError`).
- Relative offsets: `+Nd` is N days after `today`, `+0d` is `today`. Negative or unsigned offsets (`-3d`, `3d`) raise `InvalidDate`.
- `today` and `tomorrow` keep working; matching stays case-insensitive and ignores surrounding whitespace.

Only edit what this ticket needs. Other tickets (TT-102 to TT-104) are being done in parallel by other items; do not implement them.
